label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Hey Mikaela, good on you for asking properly. We owe you after Dave's shoulder, so here's the honest version.

We're milking 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept, just after mating started. We skip Tues, Thurs and Sat arvo, plus Sunday arvo, so that's four once-a-days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day.

Production: milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. The rep had said to expect 8-10, so we're at the better end of that, but it's still a real drop and I'm not going to dress it up.

Cells did go up. We went from about 110k to around 180k in the first three weeks. It's back down to about 135k now, but that first bit scared me, so I'd be watching the vat closely and having a yarn with your vet about it.

The good stuff: lame cows are way down. We've got 4 on the lame list now against 11 this time last year. We've got a 1.8km walk to the back paddocks and I reckon having fewer trips to and from the shed helps a lot with that. The cows also came round quicker than I expected. They bellowed at the gate for about four days and then they were fine.

The hours are the big one for us. Sunday arvo was the first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years, and Dave and I drove to Hamilton to see the grandkids. Kieran, our 2IC, reckons it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. Honestly, that counts for a lot.

Now the bad bits, because you asked for them:

- We had a heifer get mastitis on a skipped arvo. I didn't spot it until the next morning and we lost a quarter. That one's on me, and it's the main reason I'd say the checking has to be spot on.
- You've got to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days, or it bites you. There's no slack in it.
- The milk drop and the cell bump are both real, and I wouldn't tell you otherwise.

My honest take is that I wouldn't go back. For us the hours alone are worth the 6%. But I'd only say that if you've got the staff and the discipline to do the checks on skip days every time. Don't do it just because we did. Your situation might be different from ours.

If Tom's knees are bad, the arvos off will help more than anything else you could do.

Come and look at the shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th at the Kerrisons. I'll have them there. Or ring me if you want to talk it through, that's easier than texting with these thumbs.
